with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. The full explanations,

## Key terms

{{< glossary boolean-algebra logical-equivalence de-morgan-laws distributive-law absorption-law tautology contradiction guard-clause operator-precedence >}}

## 18.1 Calculating with 1 and 0

- True = **1**, false = **0**.
- NOT p = 1 − p; p AND q = p × q; p OR q = p + q, with 1 + 1 = 1.
- Dock door p ∧ (q ∨ r) with p = 1, q = 0, r = 1: 1 × (0 + 1) = 1, open.

![True = 1, false = 0.](images/bool-arith.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
In Boolean algebra, 1 + 1 = 1.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Calculate"}
With p = 1, q = 0, r = 0: compute p ∨ (q ∧ r), (p ∨ q) ∧ r and ¬p ∨ ¬q.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Numbers"}
p = 1, q = 0, r = 0. Choose the value.

::: {.match extra="2|−1"}
p ∨ (q ∧ r)
:   1

(p ∨ q) ∧ r
:   0

¬p ∨ ¬q
:   1

p ∧ q
:   0

¬q
:   1
:::
:::

## 18.2 The laws of Boolean algebra

- Identity, domination, idempotent, complement, double negation.
- Commutative and associative: order and brackets of one operator do not
  matter.
- **Distributive:** p ∧ (q ∨ r) ≡ (p ∧ q) ∨ (p ∧ r), and p ∨ (q ∧ r) ≡
  (p ∨ q) ∧ (p ∨ r).
- **Absorption:** p ∨ (p ∧ q) ≡ p.

![Laws of Boolean algebra.](images/bool-laws.png){width=90%}

{{< sim file="sims/equivalence-lab.html" poster="sims/equivalence-lab.png" title="Equivalence Lab: are two conditions the same?" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Not every law of numbers is a law of logic, and the other way round.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Check two laws"}
In **Equivalence Lab**, check the distributive and absorption laws. Then
compare p ∨ (q ∧ r) with (p ∨ q) ∧ (p ∨ r).
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Laws"}
Simplify.

::: {.match extra="q|¬p"}
p ∧ T
:   p

p ∨ T
:   T

p ∧ ¬p
:   F

p ∨ (p ∧ q)
:   p
:::
:::

## 18.3 De Morgan's laws

- **¬(p ∧ q) ≡ ¬p ∨ ¬q** and **¬(p ∨ q) ≡ ¬p ∧ ¬q**.
- The NOT goes into the brackets and AND and OR swap.
- Cannot dock: `!(hasPass && shieldsUp)` = `!hasPass || !shieldsUp`.

![De Morgan's laws.](images/de-morgan.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
¬(p ∧ q) is not ¬p ∧ ¬q: the row (T, F) differs.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Remove the NOT"}
Rewrite `!(isDay || isLit)` and `!(hasKey && !doorLocked)` without a NOT in
front of brackets.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · De Morgan"}
Choose the equivalent condition.

::: {.match extra="!isDay || !isLit|hasKey && doorLocked"}
!(hasPass && shieldsUp)
:   !hasPass || !shieldsUp

!(isDay || isLit)
:   !isDay && !isLit

!(hasKey && !doorLocked)
:   !hasKey || doorLocked

!(!a || !b)
:   a && b
:::
:::

## 18.4 Simplifying a condition

- One law per step, with its name; check the end with a truth table.
- (p ∧ q) ∨ (p ∧ ¬q) → p ∧ (q ∨ ¬q) → p ∧ T → **p**.
- ¬(¬p ∨ q) → ¬¬p ∧ ¬q → **p ∧ ¬q**.

![Simplifying step by step.](images/simplify-steps.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Do not jump two laws at once without a check.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Simplify"}
Simplify with the name of each law: p ∧ (p ∨ q); ¬(¬p ∧ ¬q);
(p ∨ q) ∧ (p ∨ ¬q).
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Simplify"}
Choose the simplest equivalent.

::: {.match extra="p ∧ q|¬p ∨ q"}
p ∧ (p ∨ q)
:   p

¬(¬p ∧ ¬q)
:   p ∨ q

(p ∨ q) ∧ (p ∨ ¬q)
:   p

¬(¬p ∨ q)
:   p ∧ ¬q

p ∨ (q ∧ ¬q)
:   p
:::
:::

## 18.5 Clear decision conditions in game code

- **Guard clause:** check at the start and `return` early; no deep nesting.
- Each guard is the NOT of one part of the condition.
- Name long conditions: `bool mayEnter = hasPass && !alarmOn;`.

![Nested ifs and guard clauses.](images/guard-clauses.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A guard leaves when the condition to go on is **false**.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Rewrite with guards"}
Rewrite with guard clauses: `if (isAlive) { if (hasAmmo && !reloading) Fire(); }`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Code"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="if (isAlive) return;|a && b || !c"}
Which guard starts a function that needs a living player?
:   if (!isAlive) return;

if (a) { if (b) { if (!c) Go(); } } as one condition?
:   a && b && !c

!(isDead || !hasAmmo) simplified?
:   !isDead && hasAmmo

Why name a condition with a bool?
:   the rule becomes readable
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Code Cleaner {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

The code of **Star Dock** has six strange conditions. Replace each one with
the **simplest equivalent** condition.

{{< sim file="sims/code-cleaner.html" poster="sims/code-cleaner.png" title="Code Cleaner: the simplest equivalent condition" kind="game" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Clean lines"}
Choose the simplest equivalent.

::: {.match extra="!hasPass|alarm && docked"}
!(!hasPass)
:   hasPass

hasPass && true
:   hasPass

docked || (docked && alarm)
:   docked

!(alarm || docked)
:   !alarm && !docked
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · Name the law (harder)"}
Which law does the step use?

::: {.match extra="identity|commutative"}
!(a && b) → !a || !b
:   De Morgan

(p && q) || (p && r) → p && (q || r)
:   distributive

docked || (docked && alarm) → docked
:   absorption

!(!hasPass) → hasPass
:   double negation
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- True = 1, false = 0; AND is ×, OR is + with 1 + 1 = 1, NOT is 1 − p.
- The laws rewrite a condition without changing its value.
- De Morgan: the NOT goes into the brackets and AND and OR swap.
- Simplify one law at a time, then check with a truth table.
- Guard clauses and named conditions make game decisions clear.
